precepts.text: They gave me vinegar to drink. Let their table become a snare, and that which should have been for their welfare a trap; let their eyes be darkened, that they see not. Christ speaking through David about the rulers.
precepts.point: Behold, I lay in Zion a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner stone. Their covenant with death shall be disannulled. Today that covenant is the Christian pastors and Black politicians in bed with America, as the rulers then were in bed with Rome; and 'the report' they will not understand is Isaiah 53:1, that Christ is Messiah.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
Isaiah says the word came to the rulers “that they might go, and fall backward, and be broken, and snared, and taken.” David shows the same snare. “They gave me also gall for my meat; and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.” This is a writing of David, but it is Christ speaking through David regarding himself on the cross.

“Let their table become a snare before them: and that which should have been for their welfare, let it become a trap.” Let the rulers' table be a snare. That is why Isaiah said they would be snared, trapped, broken and stumble.

“Let their eyes be darkened, that they see not”: let the eyes of the elders, the rulers, be darkened, whereunto they were appointed, so that they see not the Messiah standing in front of them. When he walked on the earth they said, that's not the guy, it can't be him. The rest of the verse: “and make their loins continually to shake.”

So the prophecy of Isaiah 28 is in reference to the elders, the leaders that ruled us. They hated God and they hated their people, and the words of God through the prophets were darkened to them.

precepts.text: Let their table become a snare before them, and let their eyes be darkened.
precepts.point: They are drunken, but not with wine; the Lord hath closed your eyes, the prophets and seers hath he covered.

note.label: All Skinfolk Ain't Kinfolk: Children of Darkness

precepts.why:
The Lord closed the eyes of the rulers, and David prays it over them: “Let their table become a snare before them: and that which should have been for their welfare, let it become a trap.” The table is the Bible. Let the Bible be a trap and a snare for the wicked of my people.

“Let their eyes be darkened, that they see not; and make their loins continually to shake.” That is the elders, the leaders, the rulers. Their minds are lost: they read the Bible and cannot understand what they are reading, because they are too rebellious and evil.

“Pour out thine indignation upon them, and let thy wrathful anger take hold of them. Let their habitation be desolate; and let none dwell in their tents.” Why? “For they persecute him whom thou hast smitten; and they talk to the grief of those whom thou hast wounded.” That is Christ: they spoke evil of him whom God smote and wounded.

That is Isaiah 29: drunken, but not with wine; the spirit of deep sleep poured out on them; the prophets, rulers and seers covered. The very book that should have been for their welfare became their snare.

precepts.text: Fear God and keep His commandments, for this is the whole duty of man; for God shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether good or evil.
precepts.point: Nothing is hid from God. Whether it be good or evil, He brings every secret thing into judgment.
precepts.why:
“O God, thou knowest my foolishness; and my sins are not hid from thee.” Nothing is hid from God. “Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man. For God shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether it be good, or whether it be evil.”

Whether it be good or evil, he brings every secret thing into judgment. That is why David does not try to hide his foolishness; his sins are not hid from the Most High, and the whole duty of man is to fear God and keep his commandments.

precepts.text: Keep and do the statutes, for this is your wisdom in the sight of the nations, who will say surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people; for what nation is so great, who hath God so nigh unto them.
precepts.point: Hear me speedily; draw nigh unto my soul and redeem it; deliver me because of mine enemies.
precepts.why:
“Hear me, O Lord; for thy lovingkindness is good”. When we call on God we want him to hear us. It is not pleasant to call on God and have him tell you, as in Hosea 5:15, that he will return to his place till you acknowledge your offence. Moses shows what keeps him near: “Keep therefore and do them; for this is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the nations, which shall hear all these statutes, and say, Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people.”

“For what nation is there so great, who hath God so nigh unto them, as the Lord our God is in all things that we call upon him for?” Keeping and doing the statutes is what has God so nigh unto us in all things we call upon him for. That is how David can say hear me speedily, draw nigh unto my soul and redeem it, deliver me because of mine enemies.

precepts.text: The dead were judged out of the books according to their works, and whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.
precepts.point: Add iniquity unto their iniquity, and let them not come into Thy righteousness; let them be blotted out of the book of the living and not be written with the righteous. That is a heavy statement.
precepts.why:
“Let them be blotted out of the book of the living, and not be written with the righteous.” That is a heavy statement. John sees what it means: “I saw the dead, small and great, stand before God; and the books were opened: and another book was opened, which is the book of life: and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works.” Then: “whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.”

David asks that the Most High pour out his indignation on them that persecute him whom he has smitten, add iniquity unto their iniquity and let them not come into his righteousness. This is why blindness happened to the southern Kingdom leadership that forsook Christ; their eyes were darkened and their table became a snare, as you read in Romans 11. To be blotted out of the book of the living is to not be found written in the book of life, and that is the lake of fire.

precepts.text: This is the love of God, that we keep His commandments, and His commandments are not grievous.
precepts.point: The seed of His servants shall inherit it, and they that love His name shall dwell therein. Those that keep the commandments are going to dwell there.
precepts.why:
David closes the psalm with the promise: “For God will save Zion, and will build the cities of Judah: that they may dwell there, and have it in possession.” Only the oppressed need to be saved, and that is us. Then he says who will dwell there: “The seed also of his servants shall inherit it: and they that love his name shall dwell therein.”

John tells us what it means to love his name: “For this is the love of God, that we keep his commandments: and his commandments are not grievous.” Loving the Most High is not a feeling; it is keeping his commandments, and they are not too heavy to bear.

So those that love his name in Psalm 69 are those that keep the commandments. They are the ones who are going to dwell in Zion when God saves it and builds the cities of Judah again.

precepts.text: David prophesied that their table would become a snare to the enemies.
precepts.point: The word became a snare upon the leadership because the understanding is given precept upon precept, in another tongue, so that those without it stumble and fall.

note.label: Isaiah 8: Maher-shalal-hash-baz, the Snare, and the Law and the Testimony

precepts.why:
Here is David’s own word that Paul quotes: “Let their table become a snare before them: and that which should have been for their welfare, let it become a trap.”

David prophesied that their table would become a snare to the enemies. That which should have been for their welfare, the word that is a sanctuary to his people, became a trap, a stone of stumbling and a rock of offence, to the leadership that rejected him when Christ came teaching. The understanding is given precept upon precept, in another tongue, so those without it stumble and fall.

precepts.text: For the zeal of thine house hath eaten me up.
precepts.point: His disciples remembered that it was written, The zeal of thine house hath eaten me up. He was fulfilling what David had written.

note.label: John 2: The First Miracle and the Cleansing of the Temple

precepts.why:
David wrote it: “For the zeal of thine house hath eaten me up; and the reproaches of them that reproached thee are fallen upon me.” When Christ made a scourge of small cords and drove them all out of the temple, with the sheep and the oxen, poured out the changers' money and overthrew the tables, his disciples remembered that it was written, “The zeal of thine house hath eaten me up.”

He was fulfilling what David had written. He drove grown men out with a whip, and said unto them that sold doves, “Take these things hence; make not my Father’s house an house of merchandise.” No man had business trading in there at the passover. That is the zeal of his Father's house eating him up, exactly as the psalm says.

note.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time

points: Save me, O God, for the waters are come in unto my soul; I sink in deep mire where there is no standing, come into deep waters where the floods overflow me.
I am weary of my crying, my throat is dry, my eyes fail while I wait for my God. They that hate me without a cause are more than the hairs of my head.
O God, Thou knowest my foolishness, and my sins are not hid from Thee.
Nothing is hid from God. Whether it be good or evil, He brings every secret thing into judgment.
Let not them that wait on Thee be ashamed for my sake, nor those that seek Thee be confounded, O God of Israel.
For Thy sake I have borne reproach; shame hath covered my face. I am become a stranger unto my brethren and an alien unto my mother's children, for the zeal of Thine house hath eaten me up.
When I wept and chastened my soul with fasting, that was to my reproach; I made sackcloth my garment and became a proverb to them.
They that sit in the gate speak against me, and I was the song of the drunkards.
But my prayer is unto Thee, O Lord, in an acceptable time; in the multitude of Thy mercy hear me, in the truth of Thy salvation.

We may think the Lord does not hear us. That is why in the fullness of time God sent His son. In the Christian church they say He may not come when you want Him, but He is always on time; the Lord comes in an acceptable time.
Deliver me out of the mire, and let me not sink; let me be delivered from them that hate me and out of the deep waters. Deliver me from the haters, and let not the deep swallow me up.
Hear me, O Lord, for Thy lovingkindness is good; turn unto me according to the multitude of Thy tender mercies, and hide not Thy face from Thy servant, for I am in trouble.
Hear me speedily; draw nigh unto my soul and redeem it; deliver me because of mine enemies.
Thou hast known my reproach, my shame, and my dishonour; mine adversaries are all before Thee. Reproach hath broken my heart, and I am full of heaviness.

Do not give yourself to heaviness, because heaviness and sorrow have killed many people. Through faith and comfort of the scriptures you will have hope, because in this walk you look to this person and that person for comfort and find none. We have to deliver our own soul by our own righteousness.
I looked for some to take pity, but there was none, and for comforters, but I found none. They gave me gall for my meat, and in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink. This goes into Christ.
Let their table become a snare before them, and that which should have been for their welfare, let it become a trap.

You can read about this in Isaiah 28: the word became precept upon precept and became a snare and a trap unto them, and they went backwards, because we bring out the understanding of the Bible but people do not want to hear it. You think you are a Christian and good with God going to church every Sunday, but it does not work like that.
Let their eyes be darkened that they see not.
Pour out Thine indignation upon them, and let Thy wrathful anger take hold of them; let their habitation be desolate.
Add iniquity unto their iniquity, and let them not come into Thy righteousness; let them be blotted out of the book of the living and not be written with the righteous. That is a heavy statement.
But I am poor and sorrowful; let Thy salvation, O God, set me up on high. I will praise the name of God with a song and magnify Him with thanksgiving.

This shall please the Lord better than an ox or bullock, because He loves obedience more than sacrifice. The humble shall see this and be glad, for the Lord heareth the poor and despiseth not His prisoners.
Let the heaven and earth praise Him, the seas and everything that moveth therein. When you read the Three Holy Children, all the creation praises God.
For God will save Zion and will build the cities of Judah, that they may dwell there and have it in possession. Only the oppressed need to be saved, and that is us.
The seed of His servants shall inherit it, and they that love His name shall dwell therein. Those that keep the commandments are going to dwell there.
